column1: # *** THERE ARE TWO NAAIRS DATABASES AND THIS ARCHIVE'S NILS WERE TAKEN WITHOUT KNOWING IT. ***
# Raised 27 September 2026 by a peer session working the Booyzen archive, relayed with a measurement
# of this archive's exposure. THE PEER SAID PLAINLY IT HAD NOT VERIFIED THE CLAIM AND THAT IT SHOULD
# BE TREATED AS REPORTED. It was verified here before anything was changed.
field
# ---------------- WHAT WAS CLAIMED, AND WHAT WAS CHECKED ----------------
the claim as received
column2: that NAAIRS now has TWO databases; that the old complete one answers 503; that the new one works but is only part of the collection because migration is still running; and therefore that a nil from the working database is not a nil.

column1: *** VERIFIED AT NARSSA'S OWN PAGE, NOT FROM THE PEER AND NOT FROM A SEARCH SNIPPET ***
column2: nationalarchives.gov.za/node/737, "Using the Search Function", read 27 September 2026: "The National Archives and Records Service of South Africa (NARSSA) is in the process of migrating MORE THAN 8.3 MILLION ENTRIES from the old NAAIRS database to the new database and therefore 'fulltext search' (new database) WILL NOT DISPLAY ALL THE RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM. In the meantime NARSSA makes BOTH DATABASES AVAILABLE for use by the public. Using the 'Search Old NAAIRS database' WILL PROVIDE A MORE COMPLETE SEARCH, while by utilising 'Search New database' the public and participating institutions are..." THE CLAIM IS THE ARCHIVE SERVICE'S OWN WORDS.

column1: and the endpoints were probed here too
column2: 27 September: www.national.archsrch.gov.za/sm300cv/smws/sm300dl answers 503 over http and nothing over https; nationalarchives.gov.za/naairs.htm is now 404; the main site answers 200. THE OLD SERVICE IS DOWN AND THE OLD PORTAL PAGE IS GONE, which matches what the peer described.

column1: # ---------------- *** WHY IT CUTS ACROSS EVERY BOUND THIS ARCHIVE WROTE *** ----------------
the distinction, and the peer put it better than this archive had
column2: EVERY NAAIRS BOUND HERE IS ABOUT THE INDEX'S COVERAGE OF THE RECORDS — which series are indexed at item level, where the estate index stops, that individual naturalisation files are not indexed and so those nulls are worth nothing. THOSE ARE GOOD BOUNDS AND THEY ARE UNAFFECTED. NOT ONE OF THEM IS ABOUT THE DATABASE'S COVERAGE OF THE INDEX, because on 15-16 September there was no reason to think a database could be partial. That is a second axis and it was invisible.

column1: # ---------------- WHICH DATABASE ACTUALLY ANSWERED — EVIDENCE, NOT PROOF ----------------
what points to the OLD complete one
column2: THE VOCABULARY OF THESE SEARCHES IS THE OLD DATABASE'S. The rows say "all repositories", "all repositories and national registers", "central-government database", and the repository code RSAE. THE NEW FULLTEXT SEARCH HAS NO SUCH REPOSITORY SELECTION. And the 16 September searches name the endpoint www.national.archsrch.gov.za/sm300cv/smws/sm300dl — sm300 is the classic SEARCH MANAGER service, which is the old one, and it is the one returning 503 today.

column1: what is NOT established
column2: THE 15 SEPTEMBER SEARCHES. Row 140 records only that "the NAAIRS entry point this archive had used throughout stopped resolving" on 16 September and that the service had moved; THE PRE-MOVE URL WAS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN. So for the three nils of 15 September the database cannot be identified from this archive's own record. THAT IS A RECORD-KEEPING FAILURE AND IT IS THE REASON THE BOUND IS NEEDED.

column1: so what was done
column2: A BOUND ADDED TO SIX NEGATIVES rather than eight — see the correction below — saying what is now known about the two databases, what the balance of evidence says about which one answered, and that this archive did not check. THE NILS ARE NOT WITHDRAWN. They are bounded, which is the honest move and costs nothing.

column1: # ---------------- *** AND A CORRECTION TO THE PEER, WHICH IS OWED BOTH WAYS *** ----------------
*** THE PEER LISTED EIGHT. ONLY SIX ARE NAAIRS NILS THAT NEED THIS BOUND. ***
column2: ITS INVENTORY WAS OTHERWISE EXACT — eight rows, right dates, right wording, so it had genuinely read this data rather than guessed. But: the row "No spelling of Ivone's maiden name in a South African naturalisation notice, 1930-1960" IS NOT A NAAIRS SEARCH AT ALL. Its method field reads "gazettes.africa full-text, South African issues only, every year from 1930 to 1960 inclusive" — a different instrument entirely, unaffected by the migration. And the row "WITHDRAWN — 'NAAIRS is down' was wrong" is ALREADY A WITHDRAWAL and carries no live claim to bound.

column1: the one the peer said to bound first was right
column2: No Leibholz appears anywhere in the South African archives is the broadest of them and the one a reader would lean on hardest. It is bounded.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE PEER HANDED BACK A CORROBORATION THIS ARCHIVE HAD NOT COUNTED ----------------
*** THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN 16 SEPTEMBER NOTE RECORDS THE OUTAGE, FROM BEFORE ANYBODY KNEW THERE WAS A MIGRATION BEHIND IT ***
column2: The gazettes.africa row — the one that is NOT a NAAIRS negative — carries this in its bound, written 16 September: "IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE SAB NATURALISATION AND ALIEN-REGISTRATION FILES THEMSELVES, WHICH ARE INDEXED ON NAAIRS AND WERE NOT SEARCHED BECAUSE NAAIRS WAS UNREACHABLE ON THE DAY." Verified verbatim here. CONTEMPORANEOUS, DATED, AND WRITTEN FOR AN ENTIRELY DIFFERENT PURPOSE, which is what makes it worth more than a memory.

column1: *** AND READING IT AGAINST ROW 22 RECONCILES A TENSION NOBODY HAD NOTICED ***
column2: On 16 September this archive recorded BOTH that "NAAIRS was unreachable on the day" AND that four variant-spelling searches were run "on the corrected endpoint". THOSE LOOK LIKE THEY CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE. Row 140 reconciles them and the order matters: the entry point used throughout STOPPED RESOLVING, the service was then found to have MOVED to www.national.archsrch.gov.za/sm300cv/smws/sm300dl, and the searches were run on the new address. THE DAY IS NOT HOMOGENEOUS — it has a before and an after, and the gazettes bound was written in the before.

column1: what that does to the identification, and it is a strengthening not a clearance
column2: IT PUTS THE 16 SEPTEMBER NILS ON sm300 BY THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN TIMELINE and not merely by their vocabulary. sm300 is the classic Search Manager, the old complete database. AND IT MAKES THE 15 SEPTEMBER NILS LIKELIER TO BE THE SAME: row 140 describes a SERVICE THAT MOVED, not a database that changed, so the pre-move entry point was in all probability the same old database at an older address. A URL move does not swap a corpus. *** THAT IS STILL INFERENCE AND THE BOUND STANDS UNCHANGED. *** The pre-move URL was never written down, and this archive does not clear a nil on a reconstruction however tidy.

column1: the general lesson, which is about auditing dates rather than about South Africa
column2: A DATED NIL IS NOT ATOMIC. This archive had been treating "16 September" as one state of the world when it contained an outage, a discovery and a migration. ANYONE AUDITING DATED SEARCHES AGAINST AN INSTRUMENT THAT MOVED SHOULD LOOK FOR A CHANGE WITHIN THE DAY, not just between days.

column1: the cheap test, when the old database answers again
column2: RE-RUN THE SIX ON THE OLD DATABASE EXPLICITLY, recording the URL this time. Until then the old service is 503 and the new one is by NARSSA's own statement incomplete, SO THERE IS NO INSTRUMENT AVAILABLE THAT CAN CLEAR THESE NILS. That is a fact about a service and is recorded once.

column1: and one rule earned, which is general and not about South Africa
column2: AN INSTRUMENT CAN BE PARTIAL WITHOUT SAYING SO AT THE POINT OF SEARCH. This archive has spent a fortnight asking whether an index covers the records. IT HAD NOT THOUGHT TO ASK WHETHER THE DATABASE COVERS THE INDEX. Record the endpoint with every nil, not just the query.
